text:
amelia_support: heads up — acme_ops hit a big wave of 429s after a marketing campaign this morning. they say it looks like bursts, not steady traffic. can someone help triage?

acme_ops: yep. we ramped from ~50 rps to ~600 rps over ~2 minutes. client saw a mix of 200s and 429s. attached a curl snippet and the response headers we got. this is in prod (hosted) against model: redwood-open-7b-v1.

acme_ops: ```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-open-7b-v1","input":"summarize...","max_tokens":512}'
```

acme_ops: response sample:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 14:02:13 GMT
X-Request-Id: rq_abc123
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1800
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 164
Retry-After: 5
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "message": "per-model RPM exhausted" }

amelia_support: thanks — that X-RateLimit-Limit / Remaining look like an RPM window (1800/min => 30 rps sustained). they hit a short burst to 600 rps so bursts easily chew through the minute quota.

mike_oncall: quick checklist: 1) is this per-model RPM or account-wide? 2) concurrency limits might also be in play for long-context requests. 3) are they sending long contexts that increase token consumption per request?

acme_ops: quick answers: 1) we used a single model ID in all requests. 2) we do a lot of 6k-token contexts for few calls. 3) we didn't see 503s, only 429s.

ingrid_ml: long contexts matter. our serving runtime charges by token, and the rate limiter backends track both requests-per-minute (RPM) and tokens-per-minute (TPM) on a per-model basis. big contexts -> higher TPM usage -> faster depletion of burst allowance. also, max concurrency caps can trigger soft-throttles that return 429 with different error messages depending on the throttle type.

amelia_support: can you repro a small sequence locally? ask them to run a controlled ramp with the header logging. we usually ask for: request payload size, tokens per request, request rate curve (rps over time), and response headers for a sample 429.

acme_ops: repro script they ran: ```python
import requests, time
url='https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate'
headers={'Authorization':'Bearer sk-xxxx','Content-Type':'application/json'}
for rps in [50,200,400,600]:
    for i in range(60):
        requests.post(url,json={"model":"redwood-open-7b-v1","input":"x","max_tokens":512},headers=headers)
        time.sleep(1.0/rps)
    print('done',rps)
```

acme_ops: outcome: at ~400->600 ramp we started seeing 429s within 30s. 10-20% of calls get 200s, others 429. Retry-After varied 3-8s.

mike_oncall: looks like classic burst > leaky-bucket capacity. Our hosted RPM is enforced with a sliding window + short burst bucket. sustained high RPS consumes both RPM and TPM quickly. Recommend these mitigations: client-side rate limiting with token bucket, exponential backoff with jitter on 429, and a warm-up ramp instead of sudden spike. also consider splitting requests across compatible model variants (if they have access) e.g., redwood-open-7b-quant has higher concurrency allowances.

ingrid_ml: additional nuance: concurrency limits are per-connection worker and per-model parallelism. large context requests hold GPU slots longer — so even if RPM permits, concurrency can be exhausted leading to head-of-line 429s. suggest reducing max_tokens or truncating context for bursts. if they must send long contexts, reduce parallelism (queue client-side) and use streaming to free up server-side resources earlier.

amelia_support: i've asked ENG to pull the serving logs for rq_abc123 and adjacent requests. @mike_oncall can you check the infra side for short-term throttles and whether it was model-level or account-level enforcement?

ratebot: [rate-limit event] model=redwood-open-7b-v1 account=acme_ops window=60s rpm=1800 remaining=0 reset_in=164

mike_oncall: confirmed — enforcement triggered on per-model RPM shard. there was a short-lived node pressure at 14:02:12 causing slightly higher Retry-After but the primary reason is the RPM bucket. infra didn't report OOMs or model restarts.

amelia_support: recommended steps to send to customer: 1) implement client-side smoothing: limit concurrency to ~30 qps and use a token bucket at 30 rps with burst capacity 100 for short tolerance. 2) add exponential backoff with jitter on 429s (start 100ms, cap 8s). 3) reduce context length where possible or precompute embeddings to shrink input. 4) request a quota increase: include ramp profile and business justification.

acme_ops: if we ask for quota increase, what numbers should we request? we want to handle occasional campaigns that hit 600 rps for ~5 mins.

ingrid_ml: rough calc: 600 rps * 60s = 36k requests/min. but if each request is 500 tokens, TPM is 18M tokens/min which is huge. more useful calc: target sustained baseline + burst headroom. if bursts are 5 mins, ask for a temporary Dedicated burst or increase RPM to 36k/min (540 rps) and corresponding TPM. also propose a rolling increase: start with 2x current RPM and monitor.

mike_oncall: note we can also propose moving to Redwood Dedicated for guaranteed reserved capacity if they have predictable heavy campaigns. Dedicated supports much higher concurrency and predictable latency and a separate quota system.

amelia_support: for immediate help i can open a short-term quota bump (manual) if they share exact token/request numbers and campaign window. acme_ops: can you paste your production token-per-request average and expected peak duration?

acme_ops: avg tokens/request ~ 700 (context + generations), peaks last ~7 minutes. we'll DM the detailed telemetry.

mike_oncall: action items: 1) amelia — offer temporary manual RPM/TPM bump and advise ingress smoothing 2) ingrid — add note to model docs re: long-context concurrency implications and example client configs 3) acme_ops — provide telemetry so we can size the bump.

ingrid_ml: I'll add an internal note to product docs: practical guidance: per-model RPM/TPM exist, max concurrency per model is typically lower for large-context workloads, and clients should prefer streaming and request batching where possible. will draft a short FAQ snippet.

amelia_support: thanks everyone. acme_ops — i'll create the support ticket with follow-ups and post the ticket link here once the manual bump is applied. :thumbsup:

acme_ops: thanks all — this is actionable. appreciate the fast turnaround. :pray:
